caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Diamond Truck Sales, Inc.
claims: Fraudulent Concealment, Intentional Misrepresentation, Negligent Misrepresentation, Breach of Contract, UCL §17200, Rescission & Restitution, Declaratory Relief
status: Active — Default ENTERED against Diamond Truck Sales, Inc.; default prove-up hearing requested at/after CMC; Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. served July 1, 2026, response deadline July 31, 2026, no appearance; Alpine Request for Entry of Default/Court Judgment and Declaration pre-drafted, execution date August 1, 2026, ready to file once Alpine's deadline lapses; CM-110 Case Management Statement filed July 20, 2026; CMC 08/12/2026, 8:30 AM, Dept. 11B
defendants: Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. (California corporation operating at multiple locations including Texas and South Carolina); Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. (California corporation; 1201 S Soderquist Road, Turlock, CA 95380); DOES 1-20
causes: Violation of Unfair Competition Law, B&P Code §17200 (Count 5)
key_facts: On April 4, 2023, Plaintiff purchased a 2014 Volvo VNL diesel semi-truck (VIN: 4V4NC9EH6EN142206) from Diamond for $26,900.00 (total charges $27,092.75) with >$12,000 down payment and remaining balance financed by third-party lender. At time of sale, truck suffered a severe DEF/emissions system defect affecting the selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system, rendering it non-compliant with California emissions regulations and unsafe for highway operation. Diamond concealed and failed to disclose: (1) the emissions defect; (2) truck's regulatory non-compliance; (3) prior owner's written/verbal disclosure of DEF system failure and engine derate condition to Diamond before resale; (4) California enforcement agency's out-of-service order. Prior owner expressly disclosed the defect to Diamond; Diamond possessed actual knowledge but sold truck to Plaintiff without disclosure. Shortly after purchase while operating under Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement, truck experienced catastrophic emissions failure, entered 'limp mode,' emitted excessive black smoke, became incapable of exceeding approximately 35 mph, rendering it commercially unusable and unsafe. Plaintiff unable to mitigate by renting/purchasing replacement vehicle due to capital exhaustion. Per the Declaration in Support of Default Judgment (Attachment 4b to the July 20, 2026 CM-110 Case Management Statement), documented out-of-pocket losses total $20,218.65: deposit (Retail Buyer's Order) $12,345.10; GAP Addendum enrollment $1,895.00; CA DMV fees $3,442.00 (billed, outstanding, penalties accruing); Brannon Tire (emergency tire/road service) $1,197.34; Mobile Will's Truck/Auto Repair Shop $740.00; Golden Empire Towing, Inc. $562.50; Western Truck Center (lamp/parts) $36.71. Additional undocumented out-of-pocket losses (sworn testimony, no receipt) total $5,750.00: Commercial Towing (CVC §22852 storage release) $750.00; Almaraz Diesel (DEF/SCR diagnostic and repair) $5,000.00. Lost commercial income for the default prove-up is conservatively calculated at $23,400.00 (18 weeks × $1,300/week) — a deliberately conservative sworn figure distinct from the broader >$46,800 projected lost-income theory pursued against both defendants at trial. Prejudgment interest under Civ. Code §3287(a) (7%, ~3.04 years) adds $4,302.55, for a compensatory subtotal of $53,671.20, plus $25,000.00 in punitive damages under Civ. Code §3294 — a default judgment prove-up total of not less than $78,671.20 plus costs of suit, sought against Diamond alone.
procedural_status: Filed 02/13/2026 (pro se, fee waiver approved). Summons issued. Diamond Truck Sales Inc. served 03/11/2026 via POS-010; response due 04/10/2026; no response filed. Request for entry of default judgment submitted 06/15/2026 at 9:00 A.M. Diamond re-served with the Amended Summons/First Amended Complaint 05/12/2026; no response filed; DEFAULT ENTERED against Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. personally served July 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM — Mustagem Usmani (Manager), 1201 S Soderquist Road, Turlock, CA 95380; served by San Joaquin County Sheriff Deputy T. Caldwell under CCP §416.10 (corporation); documents served: Amended Summons, First Amended Complaint, Notice of Case Assignment and Notice of Hearing; POS-010 signed July 2, 2026 by Sheriff's Authorized Agent Jeff Dirkse (Levying Officer File No. 2026002577; $50 fee waived). Alpine response deadline: July 31, 2026 (CCP §412.20(a)(3)). Request for Entry of Default and Court Judgment (CIV-100) and supporting Declaration pre-drafted for Alpine, execution date August 1, 2026 — the day after Alpine's response deadline lapses — seeking default judgment against Alpine on a joint-and-several basis with Diamond in the same amount (not less than $78,671.20), on the theory that Alpine's liability as Diamond's successor-in-interest/alter ego is derivative rather than additional; ready to file once Alpine's default is confirmed. No meet-and-confer outreach received from any defendant as of July 20, 2026 (meet-and-confer inapplicable per CM-110 — neither defendant has appeared). Request for Default Judgment pre-drafted and ready to file upon expiration of Alpine's response period. Case assigned to Hon. Robert T. Waters, Department 11B for all purposes including trial. Case Management Statement (CM-110) filed July 20, 2026: confirms default entered against Diamond and requests the Court conduct a default prove-up hearing against Diamond at or in connection with the CMC; discovery complete; case exempt from judicial arbitration/civil mediation because both defendants are in default or have not appeared (no opposing party available for ADR); 1-day jury trial estimate. Case Management Conference: 08/12/2026, 8:30 AM, Dept. 11B. Jury trial demanded. POST-JUDGMENT COLLECTION PREP (as of July 29, 2026 — no judgment entered yet): EJ-001 (Abstract of Judgment), EJ-130 (Writ of Execution), AT-138/EJ-125 (Debtor Examination), and MC-012 (Memorandum of Costs) are pre-drafted with the fixed case/party/court facts filled in, ready to complete the same day or next business day once judgment actually enters — judgment-dependent fields (entry date, amount, hearing dates) are intentionally left blank rather than assumed. Alpine's joint-and-several liability runs through its own pre-drafted default judgment packet (CIV-100, execution date Aug. 1, 2026) — not a CCP §187 motion to amend the judgment to add an alter ego. §187 amendment is the wrong vehicle here: it exists to add an alter ego who was never a named party, and courts generally decline to use it where the underlying judgment was entered by default (no participation by the added party to satisfy due process). Alpine is already a named, personally-served defendant pursuing its own default judgment, so no §187 motion is needed or appropriate. DEFAULT JUDGMENT PACKET REVIEW (Jul. 29, 2026): (1) CASE NUMBER ERROR — Diamond's CIV-100 (submitted 6/15/26) and Alpine's CIV-100 (pre-drafted, not yet filed) both show case number "STK-CV-UF-2026-1094" (missing the leading zeros of the actual "STK-CV-UF-2026-0001094") in every field where it appears; same defect was in the [Proposed] Judgment (JUD-100), now corrected in the file above. Diamond's CIV-100/Declaration were already submitted with this error — confirm with the clerk that the case was docketed correctly, since editing this record copy doesn't change what's already on file with the court; fix Alpine's copy before it's filed Aug. 1. (2) JUD-100 STRUCTURAL GAP — original draft's Item 5a ("against defendant (names)") named only Diamond; Alpine's joint-and-several liability appeared solely in freeform Item 8 text, which the abstract of judgment (EJ-001) and writ (EJ-130) are not built to read — corrected version above adds Alpine to Item 5a and the DEFENDANT caption. (3) OSMANI vs. USMANI — Alpine's own Declaration ISO Default Judgment (¶6) cites "the same Osmani family ownership and management" as evidentiary support for the alter-ego/successor theory, but the only individual named anywhere in the service record is Usmani (spelled both "Mustagem" and "Mustaqem" across filings) — never "Osmani." This is a sworn statement supporting Alpine's liability that doesn't match the record; confirm and correct before it's relied on further. (4) STANDING QUESTION — the Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement underlying the $23,400 lost-income claim (Exhibit 4) is contractually between Gobbato Builders, LLC and "Altamont Freight LLC" (a separate registered business entity, per its own W-9 and Amazon Relay driver roster, at a different Modesto address), not personally Brendan Ngwa Nforbi — the Declaration frames the loss as his personally. Unlikely to be caught in an uncontested default prove-up, but worth resolving (e.g., confirming sole-member/alter-ego status) before this is relied on in a contested posture. (5) DMV fee vs. use-tax exemption — the $3,442 DMV fee claimed in full as damages includes ~$2,421 in CA use/city-use tax that a CDTFA exemption request (in the same exhibit set) sought to avoid on the ground the truck "was purchased outside of California"; the Declaration doesn't disclose whether that exemption was ever granted, which could reduce the true out-of-pocket DMV obligation.
damages: $78,671.20 - $150,000+: Default judgment prove-up against Diamond alone (per sworn Declaration, Attachment 4b to the July 20, 2026 CM-110) totals not less than $78,671.20 plus costs — $20,218.65 documented out-of-pocket losses, $5,750.00 undocumented sworn losses, $23,400.00 conservative lost commercial income (18 wks × $1,300/wk), $4,302.55 prejudgment interest (Civ. Code §3287(a), 7%), and $25,000.00 punitive damages (Civ. Code §3294). The broader case-level range extends to $150,000+ if Alpine is also held liable as Diamond's successor/alter ego and the full trial-theory lost-income figure (>$46,800, projected weekly earnings ~$1,800, continuing) is pursued rather than the conservative prove-up figure; also includes disgorgement/restitution under UCL §17200 and postjudgment interest.
risk: Strong case: Diamond's fraud/concealment clearly pleaded; prior owner's disclosure to Diamond establishes knowledge; catastrophic defect objectively documented; damages quantifiable. Default judgment risk eliminated if Diamond responds before or at CMC. Punitive damages exposure substantial given willful conduct post-disclosure knowledge.
